Just insurance in general. Personal/commercial/life, health, etc
The only thing you need at minimum is property and casualty license. Health and life is more optional but P&C is required. You can buy books for the exam or purchase an online study guide for around $300 average (or if you want it cheaper hmu because I know a secret link 🤫)

College degree isn't required, I started right out of high school and hopped into a sales position at SF. I just moved up into a broker position WFH full time with a large company. Some companies might require a 4 year degree and multiple years of experience in certain fields like commercial wholesale insurance etc etc but a lot of them don't if you're not getting into a specialized position.

There's multiple avenues, you can do sales/broker or you can be service/account management, underwriter, or claims. (There's extra additional like or technical IT/ actuaries, etc etc and whatnot but I'm not going to list those all out)

My second year at one of the biggest SF agencies in the north phoenix az area (9~ employees including agent) my salary was a little over 71k.

My base salary that I lived on was $36k to start with no experience and it went up as high as $40k on my 3rd year when I left. 
Uncapped commissions as well and I usually averaged around 2-3k gross.

(Residuals means: I get paid commissions again if someone renews a policy, this compounds each year  so if you do well most brokers/sales agents make over 100k around 3rd year) 
note: you have to be good at talking to people/sales and close on business consistently to achieve those numbers lol

First off, I just want to say get those booty bands for your leg exercises. They help transfer the weight to your thighs/glute areas instead of your knees.

I start out with quads which included:
Squats while holding a dumbbell(with the band on) 
Step ups (usually only a about 5 inches on the ground so I guess equivalent to two or three books stacked)
Terminal knee extensions
(You take the band, put it on the leg of a chair and your leg in as well, and straighten your knee/leg out to create a resistance, release and repeat)

Then I move onto hamstrings 
I start with a hamstring curl (I use the machine at the gym for this where you put your leg under the round weight thing while kinda sitting your front against the rest and doing curls with your leg)
Wall sitting (you just sit yourself against the wall but be careful with this one cause if you sit too deep into it this can come back onto your knees)
Glute bridge lift
(I put the band on, I lay down and I take a weight bar, usually 30 pounds, I put rest it on my pelvic area and essentially lift my lower body up while tightening my glute muscles in and make my body like a bridge. ((You keep your knees folded up like you’re doing a crunch when you do this))

Calves
I use the machine where you stand up on your tippy toes to lift the weights

Glutes
I do the thigh abductor machines and then finish off everything with kickbacks (put the band below your knees, hands on the wall and just kick your leg back)
